key_insight: AssemblyWorld tests whether general-purpose pretrained agents can perform 3D assembly just by seeing parts and interacting with them, without special assembly fine-tuning. The paper’s core idea is that assembly can be framed as a visual-interactive task in a controlled environment, revealing how far general agents can go on spatial reasoning.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between recognizing 3D parts and actually assembling them into correct spatial configurations. It tackles the challenge of evaluating whether existing pretrained agents can understand part relationships, follow assembly instructions, and perform precise manipulation in 3D.
method: Introduces AssemblyWorld, an interactive 3D environment where agents inspect rendered views of parts and manipulate rigid objects.
Provides assembly tasks guided by images or assembly manuals when available, enabling instruction-conditioned evaluation.
Measures whether general-purpose agents can complete assembly through visual interaction alone, without assembly-specific fine-tuning.
impact: This matters because it benchmarks real-world spatial reasoning and manipulation for foundation models in a realistic 3D setting. For practitioners, it helps identify the limits of current agents and what capabilities are needed for robotics, CAD, manufacturing, and embodied AI.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing inputs: rendered views, manual/images, and rigid parts leading to assembly actions.
A step-by-step 3D assembly sequence illustrating part inspection, alignment, and final completion.
A comparison chart of agent performance with and without assembly-specific fine-tuning.
An icon set for perception, reasoning, manipulation, and evaluation metrics.
paper_title: AssemblyWorld: Rethinking 3D Assembly with General-Purpose Agents
paper_authors: Jiahao Zhang, Yeying Fan, Moitreya Chatterjee, Suhas Lohit, Bernhard Egger
